content:
marie_support: Customer (acme_ops) escalated — they received a burst of 429s but the Quota/Rate dashboard shows 0 usage and full quota available. Can SRE/eng take a look?

acme_ops: we hit 429s between 2025-12-10T13:02:10Z and 2025-12-10T13:07:30Z. Console shows 0/100k tokens used. Attached minimal repro: 

```
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx\" -H \"X-Request-ID: r-9f4a2e\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: r-9f4a2e
x-rate-limit: 0/100000
```

marie_support: request id r-9f4a2e, org_id=org_8acm, customer reports console shows a flat zero for usage and quota charts.

tom_sre: could be a metrics ingestion problem. @anika_eng_runtime can you check enforcement logs for org_8acm and the metrics pipeline around that time? any recent deploys to exporters/metrics-ingest?

anika_eng_runtime: checking enforcement service now — I can see throttle events for org_8acm at 13:02 with counters incrementing in enforcement logs: `throttle_event{org=\"org_8acm\"} 37`. However, the metrics collector doesn't show the corresponding `quota_consumed` time series for that org in the metrics DB.

metrics-bot: [ALERT] metrics-ingest-lag cluster-a = 42m; kafka-consumer-group=metrics-ingest stale partitions: 3

jason_product: FYI we shipped a small metrics refactor yesterday that renamed a few metric keys (quota_remaining -> quota_remaining_v2) but there was supposed to be a compatibility alias. UI queries should fallback though — if values missing it should show N/A not zero.

anika_eng_runtime: digging deeper — the exporter change included a protobuf schema bump. We had one exporter (metrics-exporter-v2) that started pushing to topic `metrics.v2` while the ingestion lambda was still subscribed to `metrics.v1` partitions for a subset of orgs due to an older consumer group assignment. Result: enforcement emits throttle logs (right), exporter wrote metrics but they landed on the wrong topic/partition for org_8acm. Some partitions overflowed briefly and the ingestion pipeline dropped batches. That explains missing timeseries and zeroed UI.

tom_sre: ok that matches the bot alert. action items: 1) reattach consumer to metrics.v2 partitions for the affected consumer group, 2) backfill dropped metrics for 13:00-13:10 using enforcement logs, 3) add alias in query layer so old metric names map to the new ones, 4) create an alert to surface UI showing zero but enforcement shows throttles.

anika_eng_runtime: I can do (1) and (2) — starting consumer reconfiguration now. For backfill, I will run a reconciliation job that converts enforcement `throttle_event` counts -> `quota_consumed` points and push to metrics-store with original timestamps. ETA ~45m.

jason_product: I'll push a hotfix to the UI to treat missing timeseries as \"data delayed\" instead of zero so customers aren't misled. Also adding a product note in console: \"If you see 0 but receive 429s contact support.\"

acme_ops: thanks team — appreciate the quick triage. Will you confirm after backfill so we can validate?

marie_support: yes — I'll keep this thread updated. Opening a SPT ticket for billing compensation after reconcilation completes (ticket SPT-6882).

metrics-bot: [INFO] consumer-reassign job started by anika_eng_runtime at 2025-12-10T13:15:10Z

anika_eng_runtime: consumer reattached, ingestion resumed. kicking off reconciliation (throttle -> quota_consumed). I'll post once backfill completes.

marie_support: thanks everyone — marking customer notified. Follow-ups: postmortem to include root cause (exporter->topic mismatch + partition overflow), missing fallback for metric name, UI misrepresentation of missing data, and an alerting gap.

acme_ops: confirmed after 13:50 — dashboard now shows correct usage and the 429 window is reflected. Thanks!

marie_support: closing the active escalation. I will add the postmortem owners: anika_eng_runtime (ingest), tom_sre (ops), jason_product (ui), marie_support (customer comms).
